lesson.title: Números de Verdad: Phone Numbers and Lunch Count
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: You've counted, listened, and done math in Spanish. Today your numbers leave the classroom: you'll practice saying a phone number and counting how many classmates are buying lunch — two things Spanish speakers do with numbers every single day.

In Spanish, a phone number isn't said as one long number — it's usually said two digits at a time, the same way you might say 'five-five-five, twelve, thirty' for 555-1230 in English. That's exactly why you spent this week learning diez, veinte, and treinta: two-digit numbers are the building blocks of a spoken phone number.

Try saying this made-up phone number two digits at a time: 5-15-20-30 becomes cinco, quince, veinte, treinta. Now try your own: pick any four numbers between cero and treinta and say them in a row, like a phone number.

Cafeterias and classrooms count things constantly — how many kids are buying lunch, how many are bringing lunch from home. Practice this real classroom question and answer:

¿Cuántos van a comprar el almuerzo hoy? (How many are buying lunch today?)
Quince van a comprar el almuerzo. (Fifteen are buying lunch.)

Count how many people are in your house right now, and answer using son: Somos cinco. (There are five of us. / We are five.)
You just used this week's numbers for two real jobs: sharing a phone number and counting a real group of people. Tomorrow you'll put everything together in one game: number bingo, cero to treinta.

objectives: Say a string of Spanish numbers the way a phone number is spoken, two digits at a time
Ask and answer ¿Cuántos van a comprar el almuerzo? using a number and son/somos
Apply this week's numbers to two genuine real-world uses instead of a classroom drill
materialsNeeded: A family member to interview and count with
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Ask the child how they'd say a phone number out loud in English, digit group by digit group.
2. Introduce the idea that Spanish phone numbers are usually said two digits at a time, which is exactly why diez, veinte, and treinta matter.
3. Practice saying a few made-up number strings aloud together, like a phone number.
4. Introduce ¿Cuántos van a comprar el almuerzo? and model an answer with son (e.g., Quince van a comprar el almuerzo).
5. Count how many people are actually in the room or house right now and answer together using Somos ___.
6. Complete the translate activity.
7. Complete the worksheet.
8. Preview tomorrow's number bingo.
differentiationTips: Struggling: keep the phone-number and lunch-count numbers to landmarks only (cero, cinco, diez, quince, veinte, veinticinco, treinta) rather than mixing in tricky teens or twenties
Ready for more: have them ask ¿Cuántos van a comprar el almuerzo? to real family members today and tally the real answers in Spanish

This lesson's phone-number and interview practice work as live spoken exchanges between the child and a family member — they don't depend on the audio-recording gap noted elsewhere this week (open decision, expansion-plan-2026-09.md §12.9)
teacherGuide.answerKey: Phone numbers in Spanish are usually said two digits at a time (e.g., 5-15-20-30 = cinco, quince, veinte, treinta). ¿Cuántos van a comprar el almuerzo? means 'how many are buying lunch?' — answer with a number + van a comprar el almuerzo, or Somos + a number for 'there are ___ of us.'
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Delivers the week's Day 4 target (real-world numbers via phone-number and lunch-count practice) under WA-WL-2015.3.1 Connections by putting the week's numbers to two uses a child already does in English — sharing a phone number and counting a group — which is the exact 'making connections' the standard names, not a new grammar point.

generationData.instructions: Answer each question about real-world Spanish numbers.

rows.problem: Write a made-up phone number using four Spanish numbers between cero and treinta, and say it out loud.
How many people live in your house? Write the answer as 'Somos ___.'
What does ¿Cuántos van a comprar el almuerzo? mean in English?
Write an answer to that question using a number: '___ van a comprar el almuerzo.'
